correctness.rationale: For every \(k\ge1\), the exact divisor-sum identity gives \(a=M(p+1)-hq<Mp<pq\), reducing possible small proper-divisor sums to \(r+sp+tq\) with \(0\le r,s,t\le M\). If \(a\ge q\) and neither of the two residual candidates is representable, there are \(1\le u,v<h\) with \(d=v-u\) and \(u\equiv h(1+d)\pmod p\). But \(h(3-h)\le h(1+d)\le h(h-1)\), whose residues modulo \(p>h^2\) cannot lie in \(\{1,\ldots,h-1\}\). This proves the critical short-residue obstruction. For \(0<a<q\) the coefficient of \(q\) vanishes, leaving exactly the claimed congruence and open rational interval. The bound and primitivity are direct inequalities proved separately. The packaged checker compares the exact classification on 186282 eligible prime pairs through \(k=10\), and also reproduces Iannucci’s published unrestricted counts; the symbolic proof, not finite checking, establishes the universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The archived 2015 source explicitly conjectures the one-third abundance upper bound, uses an exact finite enumeration criterion, and tabulates examples; it does not assert the infinite square-root-strip theorem. Melfi treats a disjoint sufficient family near twice M. The closest directly read published research record has the strictly weaker three-quarter abundance coefficient and lacks an all-q modular classification. Eight actual targeted published-finding corpus semantic queries found no stronger covering implication; the older Pajunen characterization was not directly inspectable and hidden equivalence remains a specific risk. Novelty is best-knowledge conditional on these searches and actual source comparisons, not proven by search absence.
residual_risks: Pajunen’s 1980 structural characterization is known indirectly from Melfi but a complete lawful copy was not located for full inspection; a concealed equivalent or strong corollary cannot be excluded.
Semantic database searching, even at multiple equivalent parametrizations, cannot prove uniqueness against all unindexed results.

value.rationale: This is a naturally parameterized positive-width region of Iannucci’s published open abundance conjecture, not a random finite slice: the distance of p from the Mersenne threshold controls a structural residue obstruction. For all exponents it both proves the conjectured one-third bound in this strip and determines exactly which prime cofactors q work, as an open interval intersected with h-1 prime residue classes. The result does not require a general theorem outside the strip or assert infinitude. Reproducible finite examples illustrate but do not determine its value.
